result.rationale: The diff changes the fallback in updateEvent (and deleteEvent) from `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` to `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. When externalCalendarId is absent/falsy (the very case the fallback exists for), no destination calendar can have an externalId equal to the absent value, so find() always returns undefined and the fallback yields undefined instead of a valid calendar ID — breaking updates/deletes that previously targeted the destination calendar. This is a verifiable defect introduced by this diff.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at line 254 in the diff, the code is: `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. When `externalCalendarId` is absent/falsy, this fallback searches for a destination calendar where `externalId === undefined/null`, which will never match any real calendar entry. This means when no externalCalendarId is provided, the selectedCalendar will be undefined, causing updates to potentially fail or target the wrong calendar. The same bug pattern appears at line 314 for deleteEvent. This is a real logic error in the fallback mechanism.
